## bcfefce862fd

**Finding: reproduced size-cutoff shortcut.** Generator SHA-256 `d1620bbb459a004966a2a4a65287709394d9fd163df4e13353dab397f08cb9ce` advertises and emits rectangle heights and widths only in `3..5`, while the canonical task includes lawful marker bounding boxes of `7×4`, `4×6`, and `6×3`. Therefore the wrong rule “fill the marker bbox only when both spans are at most 5; otherwise leave the markers unchanged” fits the complete documented ordinary generator domain.

The source-bound reproducer sampled 100 deterministic draws in each of easy, medium, and hard. All **300/300** inputs had both bbox spans at most 5, all 300 passed `self_check` and `strict_canonical_like`, and the wrong rival matched the actual Racket output on the retained generated example. The rival fits only **2/5** canonical pairs and is refuted by canonical train pair 2, whose `7×4` bbox passes both target validators. Exact grids, outputs, hashes, sampler, domain classification, and command are in `checks/audit_bcfefce862fd/size_cutoff_counterexample.json`; the executable reproducer is `checks/audit_bcfefce862fd/reproduce_counterexample.py`.

This gap survives otherwise strong checks: lint, mutation-sensitive self-check, 60 Racket rule-smoke applications, defect lint, profile floor, semantic gate, **13,710/13,710** sampled override draws, and selected-authority parity all passed in `checks/audit_bcfefce862fd/`. The existing semantic rivals partition square/tall/wide shape, color, placement, and diagonal, but none is conditioned on absolute span. The profile floor tracks grid dimensions and palette rather than marker-bbox dimensions.

**Scope/limitation.** The 300-draw census is finite, but the stronger conclusion follows from declared exact-axis bounds `rect_height=3..5` and `rect_width=3..5`; no ordinary valid override can request the canonical larger spans. No fix was made because this was an audit-only target.
